transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Since the crash, even small things on the road make me jump out of my skin, and I can’t bring myself to drive like I used to. It's just gotten to the point where I'm struggling to get around, and my daughter insisted I come speak to someone.
I'm so sorry you went through that crash. How long ago did the accident happen, and how long have you been experiencing these reactions?

The crash happened about a year and seven months ago. These reactions started pretty much right after, and they really haven't let up at all since then. It has been hanging over me day in and day out for this whole time.
Do you find yourself having upsetting, unwanted memories or nightmares about the crash itself? Or do you ever feel like you are actually reliving the accident?

Yes, it happens quite a bit. Out of nowhere, like if I hear a siren or see a car speed on TV, I'm right back in that intersection hearing the crunch of metal and my wife screaming. I even find myself physically gripping an imaginary steering wheel while I'm just sitting in my chair at home.
Since the accident, have you also had trouble sleeping, felt constantly on guard, or noticed that you get easily irritated?

Yes, most nights I lie awake for hours staring at the ceiling and wake up feeling exhausted, and when I'm in the car, I'm constantly scanning the mirrors and intersections on guard. I've also found myself snapping at my wife and daughter over little things like how they load the dishwasher, raising my voice before I even realize it. It makes me feel so ashamed afterward because that's just not the kind of man I used to be.
Do you find yourself actively trying to avoid thoughts, feelings, or conversations about the crash, or do you feel emotionally distant from your family since it happened?

Yes, both of those are very true for me. I avoid driving on certain roads or talking about the crash because just thinking about it makes my chest tighten up, and when my daughter and grandkids are over, I feel like I'm watching them from behind a glass wall, just going through the motions without really feeling part of things.

The avoidance of driving is a symptom of PTSD rather than an isolated Specific Phobia (F40.224), so F40.224 has been removed.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (ICD-10: F43.1) following a severe car accident that occurred approximately 19 months ago. He exhibits persistent intrusive symptoms (flashbacks, distressing memories, physiological reactivity), active avoidance of trauma-related stimuli (avoiding specific roads and discussions about the crash), negative alterations in cognition and mood (emotional detachment and estrangement from family), and marked hyperarousal (insomnia, hypervigilance, and irritability). These symptoms have persisted for well over the required one-month duration and cause significant distress and functional impairment in his daily life and family relationships.
